facts.statement: The genus Acostasaurus was described by Gómez Pérez and Noè in 2017.
facts.quote: authority: Gómez Pérez & Noè, 2017

facts.statement: Fossils of Acostasaurus date to the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Barremian~

facts.statement: Acostasaurus fossils have been found in the Barremian-aged Paja Formation in Colombia.
facts.quote: known from the Barremian of the Paja Formation, Colombia

facts.statement: The type specimen, UNDG R-1000, includes a nearly complete skull, a full hindlimb, and several vertebrae.
facts.quote: The type specimen, UNDG R-1000, is known from a near complete skull, and postcranial elements including a complete hindlimb and various vertebrae

facts.statement: The known specimen of Acostasaurus is estimated to be over 4 meters long.
facts.quote: The specimen has an estimated size of over 4 m in length

facts.statement: The type specimen features an incompletely ossified sagittal crest and undeveloped palatine wings, suggesting it may have been a subadult.
facts.quote: the sagittal crest is not fully ossified, as well as possessing undeveloped palatine wings

facts.statement: Acostasaurus had a very large scleral ring, indicating adaptation for vision in deep or murky waters.
facts.quote: The scleral ring of the specimen is also very large, suggesting that Acostasaurus was adapted to see in deep or murky waters

facts.statement: Acostasaurus possessed a short mandibular symphysis containing only six pairs of functional tooth sockets.
facts.quote: it possesses a short mandibular symphysis, containing only 6 pairs of functional alveoli

facts.statement: Acostasaurus had a heavily swollen and ornamented sagittal crest that formed a parietal knob.
facts.quote: it also possessed a heavily swollen and ornamented sagittal crest to form a parietal knob

facts.statement: Acostasaurus is distinguished from typical brachauchenine pliosaurs by its caniniform dentition rather than longirostrine homodont dentition.
facts.quote: Acostasaurus possesses caniniform dentition, whereas brachauchenines possess longirostrine homodont dentition

facts.statement: Researchers compared Acostasaurus to various brachauchenine taxa, though they found referral to that subfamily problematic.
facts.quote: Gómez Pérez et al. compared Acostasaurus to a variety of brachauchenine taxa in the paper

facts.statement: Acostasaurus is classified within the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pliosauridae

facts.statement: Acostasaurus belongs to the suborder Pliosauroidea.
facts.quote: subordo: Pliosauroidea

facts.statement: Acostasaurus was found in rocks from the Barremian (Early Cretaceous) of the Paja Formation in Colombia.
facts.quote: el cual ha sido hallado en rocas que datan de la época del Barremiense (Cretácico Inferior) de la Formación Paja, en Colombia

facts.statement: The specimen is estimated to have reached a length of about 4 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: Se estima que el espécimen alcanzaba un tamaño de unos 4 a 5 metros de longitud

facts.statement: The large scleral ring indicates that Acostasaurus was adapted to see in deep or turbid waters.
facts.quote: El anillo esclerótico del espécimen también es muy grande, lo que indica que Acostasaurus estaba adaptado a ver en aguas profundas o turbias

facts.statement: The mandibular symphysis of Acostasaurus ends halfway along the sixth pair of teeth.
facts.quote: la sínfisis termina justo a la mitad del sexto par de dientes

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the base of the functional tooth sockets in Acostasaurus merges with Meckel's canal, similar to Simolestes.
facts.quote: Gómez-Pérez et al. señalaron que la base de los alvéolos funcionales en Acostasaurus confluyen con el surco de Meckel como ocurre en Simolestes

facts.statement: Acostasaurus has caniniform dentition with a short snout, distinguishing it from the long-snouted homodont dentition of brachauchenines.
facts.quote: Acostasaurus tiene una dentadura caniniforme con un hocico corto, mientras que los bracauqueninos poseen una dentadura homodonta con un rostro alargado

facts.statement: Acostasaurus lived between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)
